meta.triageRationale: One story in one module (vscode-plugin/src/delivery) with the approach already settled by the approved mock. The task rows are built in board-details.ts (taskRows: dependsOn today maps to full titles), typed by TaskRowView in board-protocol.ts, and rendered by taskList in the BOARD_WEBVIEW_SCRIPT in board-host.ts, whose openOf map already keeps fold state per screen entry. The change gives each row its short id and dependency ids with titles, renders a table with a checks toggle, and updates the tests that pin the old details.task markup (board-host.test.ts, board-details.test.ts). A few files and tasks, but one obvious approach, so small rather than feature. Grounding is code reading plus grep of these files and a live screenshot of the current board.

findings.premise: The design covers the approved mock (/tmp/board-shot/mock.png): an ID / Task / Result / Depends on / Checks table, short-ID dependency chips, a dash when there are none, and an '<n> checks' toggle that opens the checks under the row. It also keeps the counts line.
findings.evidence: I read the mock. It shows the 'PLANNED TASKS' label, the counts line '4 passed, 0 failed, 0 unrecorded, 0 unplanned', and the header 'ID Task Result Depends on Checks'. Its rows read T001..T004 with Passed pills, chips T001/T002/T003 or '—', and toggles '▸ 8 checks' / '▾ 5 checks'. The open row lists the checks under the task. All of these appear in §2.3. [files: /tmp/board-shot/mock.png]

findings.premise: The open checks row lists the checks as a 'plain bulleted list' (§2.3 postcondition).
findings.evidence: In the mock the open T002 checks row shows plain indented lines with no bullet marks, such as 'stop cancels the provider turn…' and 'stop or detach while a turn waits…'. The design's own Summary says 'opens them as a plain list'. Only the §2.3 postcondition says 'bulleted', so the design contradicts the mock and itself. [files: /tmp/board-shot/mock.png]
findings.action: State that the checks render as an unbulleted list (ul with list-style:none and no ::before glyph), matching the mock, or confirm that bullets are wanted.

findings.premise: The ac1–ac3 acceptance criteria named in §5 trace to an upstream spec or triage record.
findings.evidence: I grepped the repo for '0184df38'. It matches only the LLD itself (docs/standalone/.../S001/LLD.md and .insrc/artifacts/LLD-0184df38314415ae-S001.json). No SPEC or triage artifact defines ac1..ac3, so I could not check the criteria's wording against an upstream source.
findings.action: Spell out ac1–ac3 in the LLD, or link the triage/spec record that defines them.

findings.premise: Today taskRows gives dependsOn as dependency titles through the sourceIds join, keeps the raw PLAN id when no task item joins, and sets dependsOn/acceptanceChecks to null when there is no ok PLAN task.
findings.evidence: board-details.ts:42 has `itemForPlanId = (planId) => taskItems.find(t => t.sourceIds.includes(planId))`. Lines 55-58 read `dependsOn: planTask === undefined ? null : planTask.dependsOn.map(d => { const dep = itemForPlanId(d); return dep === undefined ? d : titleOf(dep); })`. Line 59 reads `acceptanceChecks: planTask === undefined ? null : [...]`. Lines 45-47 find planTask only when `plan.state === 'ok'`. [files: vscode-plugin/src/delivery/board-details.ts]

findings.premise: Today taskList renders each task as a <details class='task'> whose summary is only the title (or the taskItemId), with a 'Depends on <titles>' pill and a ballot-box check list. The counts line, the 'No task plan recorded yet.' message and the planNotice follow it.
findings.evidence: board-host.ts:231-235: `make('details',undefined,'task')`, `make('summary',t.title===null?t.taskItemId:t.title)`, `pill(... 'Depends on '+t.dependsOn.join(', '),'neutral')`, and `make('ul',undefined,'checks')`. Line 228 renders task-counts, line 229 'No task plan recorded yet.', and line 235 plan-notice. CSS at board-host.ts:428 is `.checks li::before{content:"\2610  "...}`, the ballot box. One detail the design leaves out: an empty dependsOn today shows a 'No dependencies' pill, which the design replaces with a dash, as the mock shows. [files: vscode-plugin/src/delivery/board-host.ts]

findings.premise: The design reuses existing pieces with their stated shape: the .table-wrap/table.records styling (which scrolls on a narrow column), the pill helper with a tone, and openOf keyed by model.entryId.
findings.evidence: board-host.ts:237 recordsTable uses `make('div',undefined,'table-wrap')` and `make('table',undefined,'records')`. CSS lines 439-441 style table.records, and lines 452-453 set `.table-wrap{overflow-x:auto;}` and `table.records{min-width:620px;}`. Line 98 defines `pill(text,tone,cls)`. Line 103 declares `const scrollOf={},openOf={};`, and lines 160-162 and 171 key it by `model.entryId+':'+...`. The proposed key `entryId+':checks:'+taskItemId` does not collide with the stage and ':fold' keys. [files: vscode-plugin/src/delivery/board-host.ts]

findings.premise: shortId and TaskDependencyView are new. No existing helper already derives a task's short id.
findings.evidence: board-protocol.ts:122-133 TaskRowView has no shortId. compactIdOf in board-model.ts covers card ids only: board-model.test.ts:223 says 'a task id is not a card id and is returned whole'. Adding a separate last-segment rule is therefore justified. [files: vscode-plugin/src/delivery/board-protocol.ts, vscode-plugin/src/delivery/board-model.ts]

findings.premise: The rule 'shortId is the last ':'-separated segment' gives T<nnn> for every task item id the daemon mints.
findings.evidence: src/workflow/delivery/graph.ts:15 and types.ts:83 say task ids take the '<story id>:T<nnn>' form, even under a ':R(<raw>)' story (graph.test.ts:264 has `${EPIC_ID}:R(x):T002`). The last segment is therefore always T<nnn>. [files: src/workflow/delivery/graph.ts, src/workflow/delivery/types.ts]

findings.premise: The call-site inventory covers every consumer of TaskRowView.dependsOn and of the old task markup: board-protocol.ts, board-details.ts and board-host.ts, plus the tests updated in the migration steps.
findings.evidence: A grep for dependsOn/TaskRowView in vscode-plugin/src/delivery finds production uses only in board-protocol.ts:129, board-details.ts:55 and board-host.ts:233. details-memory.ts:40 uses PlanTaskView, not TaskRowView. The tests that pin the old shape or markup are board-details.test.ts:48 and :272, board-host.test.ts:442, :456, :558 and :574 (string dependsOn), and board-host.test.ts:1155-1157 and :1172 (details.task). Migration steps 1-2 say to update the view-model and host tests. The §3.1 call-site list could name those test files explicitly. [files: vscode-plugin/src/delivery/__tests__/board-details.test.ts, vscode-plugin/src/delivery/__tests__/board-host.test.ts]
findings.action: Optionally list the pinned test sites (board-details.test.ts:48,272; board-host.test.ts:442,456,558,574,1155-1157,1172) under §3.1 call sites.

findings.premise: TaskRowView is a webview-only shape and is never persisted. Fold memory (openOf) lives only in the webview session.
findings.evidence: TaskRowView is used only in ItemDetailsViewModel.tasks (board-protocol.ts:174), which is posted to the webview. details-memory.ts stores PLAN tasks (id/dependsOn/acceptanceChecks strings, line 40), not TaskRowView. openOf is a plain in-script object (board-host.ts:103). No migration is needed. [files: vscode-plugin/src/delivery/board-protocol.ts, vscode-plugin/src/delivery/details-memory.ts, vscode-plugin/src/delivery/board-host.ts]

findings.premise: When the PLAN cannot be read, the failure is detectable and handled: dependsOn and acceptanceChecks stay null, every task row remains, and planNotice renders under the table.
findings.evidence: board-details.ts:45-47 finds planTask only when plan.state==='ok', so a failed read yields null dependsOn/acceptanceChecks (lines 55, 59). board-details.ts:213 sets `planNotice: plan.state === 'failed' ? `The plan could not be read: ${plan.message}` : null`. board-host.test.ts:537-538 already checks that the notice shows and the results remain. [files: vscode-plugin/src/delivery/board-details.ts, vscode-plugin/src/delivery/__tests__/board-host.test.ts]

findings.premise: A PLAN dependency with no joining task item is detectable at the existing join and can fall back to { shortId: raw, title: raw }.
findings.evidence: board-details.ts:56-57: `const dep = itemForPlanId(d); return dep === undefined ? d : titleOf(dep);`. This undefined branch is where the raw-id pair goes. The existing fixture covers the case: board-details.test.ts:44 has `dependsOn: ['t2', 't9']`, and t9 has no task item. [files: vscode-plugin/src/delivery/board-details.ts, vscode-plugin/src/delivery/__tests__/board-details.test.ts]

findings.premise: The integration tests can run the new table and checks toggle (click, aria-expanded, showing and hiding the next row, re-render keeping it open) in the board-webview-harness fake DOM, which forbids innerHTML.
findings.evidence: board-webview-harness.ts:14 says 'A fake DOM element: records text, attributes, children, listeners and form values; innerHTML throws'. It has generic getAttribute/attrs (line 54) and querySelectorAll (line 56), and listeners are called by the click() helper (board-host.test.ts:1167). Tables already render and are asserted there (board-host.test.ts:1173-1175, the tr rows of records). [files: vscode-plugin/src/delivery/__tests__/board-webview-harness.ts, vscode-plugin/src/delivery/__tests__/board-host.test.ts]

findings.premise: Each acceptance criterion and edge case has a test.
findings.evidence: §5 maps ac1 to the board-details taskRows short-id and dependency-pair test, ac2 to the board-host five-column table test, and ac3 to the re-render persistence test. The integration subjects also cover the 'No task plan' case, '1 check' versus '<n> checks', the null-title fallback, and the evidence tab having no task rows. The unit subjects cover the no-':' id and the raw-id dependency. Two edge cases have no named subject: Back between stories keeps separate open choices, and the narrow-column scroll (whose CSS is already asserted by board-host.test.ts:1697 for .table-wrap). Both are low risk. [files: vscode-plugin/src/delivery/__tests__/board-host.test.ts]
findings.action: Optionally add a subject for per-story open choices across open → Back.

coverage-of-intent.2.note: Applied: §2.3 and the test strategy now say the checks render as a plain list with no bullet marks or checkbox glyphs, matching the mock and the summary.

coverage-of-intent.3.note: Applied: ac1-ac3 are now spelled out in the acceptance mapping. They are derived from the story spec captured at triage (the user-approved mock /tmp/board-shot/mock.png); the standalone story has no separate SPEC record.

summary.prose: A story's planned tasks on the Delivery board become a table: one row per task with its short ID, title, result, dependencies as short-ID chips (full title on hover) and a count of acceptance checks that opens them as a plain list under the row. The row model gains the task's short ID and each dependency's short ID and title, so the webview only lays them out. The counts line, the no-plan message and the plan notice stay; the checkbox glyphs that read as unticked go away.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Show a story's planned tasks as a table on the Delivery board

Each dependency is { shortId, title } from the task item it joins to (the same sourceIds join as today): shortId by the rule above, title by titleOf. A dependency with no task item keeps its raw PLAN id as both shortId and title.

returns.meaning: Appends the 'Planned tasks' label, the counts line, then either 'No task plan recorded yet.' or a .table-wrap holding table.records.tasks (aria-label 'Tasks'), then the plan notice (board-host.ts:227-235).

postconditions: Header row: ID, Task, Result, Depends on, Checks.
Each task row has data-item-id = taskItemId; ID cell is shortId; Task cell is title, or taskItemId when the title is null; Result is the existing pill with its tone.
Depends on: one neutral chip per dependency showing shortId with title as its hover title; a muted dash when dependsOn is null or empty.

Checks: a link-style button '<n> checks' (or '1 check') with aria-expanded; clicking it shows or hides the next row, which spans the remaining columns and lists the checks as a plain list: one line each, with no bullet marks and no checkbox glyphs (list-style none), as in the approved mock. With no checks (null or empty) the cell is a muted dash and there is no checks row.
The open choice is kept in openOf under model.entryId + ':checks:' + taskItemId, so a re-render (refresh) keeps it.

dataModelChanges.details: Adds shortId: string; dependsOn changes from readonly string[] | null to readonly TaskDependencyView[] | null. Webview-only protocol; nothing is persisted. The old dependency-pill and checkbox CSS (.task, .checks) is replaced by the table's own rules.

errorCases.detection: taskRows receives a PlanRead whose state is not 'ok', so no PLAN task joins to a row.
errorCases.response: dependsOn and acceptanceChecks stay null; the table still lists every task with its ID, title and result, the Depends on and Checks cells show a muted dash, and the existing plan notice renders under the table.
errorCases.userImpact: Tasks and results stay visible; only dependencies and checks are missing, with the notice explaining why.

errorCases.scenario: A PLAN dependency names a task id that no task item carries.
errorCases.detection: The sourceIds join in taskRows finds no task item for the dependency id.
errorCases.response: The dependency is { shortId: <raw id>, title: <raw id> }, shown as a chip with the raw id.
errorCases.userImpact: The reader still sees the dependency, by its PLAN id.

migration.stateBefore: taskRows (board-details.ts:40-62) gives each row dependsOn as dependency titles; taskList (board-host.ts:227-235) renders each task as a <details class='task'> with only the title in its summary, a 'Depends on <titles>' pill and a ballot-box check list (s1 bundles).
migration.stateAfter: TaskRowView carries shortId and dependsOn as { shortId, title } pairs; taskList renders a table.records tasks table with ID, Task, Result, Depends on chips and a checks toggle whose open choice is kept in openOf. The .task/.checks CSS is replaced by table rules.

migrationSteps.action: Change TaskRowView and taskRows to the new row shape and update the view-model tests.
Replace taskList's details blocks with the table, swap the task CSS, and update the host tests that pin the old markup.

migration.backwardCompat: TaskRowView is a webview-only protocol between the extension host and its own webview script, which ship together in one .vsix, so no other consumer sees the shape change. Nothing is persisted: the openOf fold memory lives only in the webview's session.

alternativesConsidered.name: Host-built short ids, webview table
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: TaskRowView gains shortId, and dependsOn becomes {shortId, title} pairs built in taskRows; the webview renders a table from them.
alternativesConsidered.approach: taskRows in board-details.ts computes each row's shortId (the last ':'-separated segment of the task item id, so E1:S001:T002 gives T002) and each dependency as { shortId, title } (the dependency's task item short id and titleOf, or the raw PLAN id for both when no task item matches). TaskRowView in board-protocol.ts carries shortId and the new dependsOn shape. taskList in BOARD_WEBVIEW_SCRIPT draws a table.records tasks table: ID, Task, Result pill, Depends on chips (shortId text, title as the hover title), and a Checks toggle button (aria-expanded) that shows or hides a following row holding the checks as a plain list; the open choice is kept in openOf under the screen entry. The counts line, the empty message and the plan notice stay where they are.
pros: The id and title rules live in the tested, vscode-free view-model code, not in webview string-built JS.
The webview stays a dumb renderer of the row model, as for every other board view.
Reuses the Records table styling, the pill helper and openOf.
cons: Changes the TaskRowView protocol shape, so tests that pin dependsOn as titles need updating.

alternativesConsidered.name: Webview derives short ids
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Keep TaskRowView as is (dependsOn titles) and derive short ids in the webview script from taskItemId and by matching titles.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Only the BOARD_WEBVIEW_SCRIPT changes: it shortens taskItemId itself and maps each dependency title back to a row by matching titles to get its short id.
pros: No protocol change; view-model tests stay as they are.
cons: Title matching is wrong when two tasks share a title or a dependency has no task item.
Puts id logic in string-built webview JS that is harder to test.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Violates correct dependency ids: title matching fails on duplicate titles and dependencies without a task item.

alternativesConsidered.name: Dependencies as task item ids
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: dependsOn carries the dependencies' full task item ids; the webview shortens them and looks titles up among the rows.
alternativesConsidered.approach: taskRows maps each dependency to its task item id (or the raw PLAN id); the webview shortens ids and finds titles by looking up the rows of the same story.
pros: Keeps one id format on the wire.
cons: A dependency outside the table has no title to show on hover.
Splits the display rule between host and webview.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Partial on the mock's hover titles (none for a dependency outside the table) and on testability (rule split across host and webview).
